title: The tank that closed the ring
pull: Sloped armor, wide tracks, a diesel heart

facts.text: The T-34 medium tank went into production in 1940 and became the backbone of the Red Army's tank force.
By 1942 it carried the long 76.2 mm F-34 gun, behind hull armor 45 mm thick sloped at 60 degrees, which protected it far better than the thickness alone suggests.
A 500 horsepower V-2 diesel engine drove it on wide tracks that coped with dirt roads and open country better than most tanks of its day.
It had a crew of four. In the cramped two man turret the commander also had to aim and fire the gun, a real handicap in a fight.
The Stalingrad Tractor Factory, one of the first two T-34 plants, kept building the tank until fighting reached it in September 1942.
In Operation Uranus T-34s spearheaded the armored thrusts that encircled the German Sixth Army. The Romanian troops in their path had no antitank guns heavier than 47 mm.
The commander problem was fixed only with the T-34-85 of 1944, whose three man turret let the commander simply command.

photoNote: Five crewmen of the Soviet 24th Tank Corps (renamed 2nd Guards Tank Corps on 26 December 1942) on the turret of a T-34, December 1942, during the Stalingrad winter offensive (the corps made the Tatsinskaya raid that month). Unknown Soviet photographer. Commons tags PD-Russia-1996 (public domain in Russia and in the US by the URAA date). Only 960 x 501 (Commons original 1024 x 534; the full size download hit Wikimedia 429s). Shows the hexagonal turret with the number 329; good for the spec photo window. Higher resolution alternative: T-34 tanks and officers of the 5th Tank Regiment, northern Crimea, October 1941, 1815 px, PD-Russia-1996 (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:T34_tanks.jpg), but it is the 1941 model and a year earlier.
photoCredit: Crewmen of the Soviet 24th Tank Corps on a T-34, December 1942. Unknown Soviet photographer, public domain.

declassified.fact: The tank's road wheels changed with the war. Rubber ran short in 1942, so factories began fitting all steel road wheels with internal springs, and Stalingrad built tanks without rubber tired wheels.
